correctness.rationale: For all real 2x2 SPD H and iid unit-circle directions, exact directional minimization whitens to a rank-one orthogonal projector. Reflection symmetry closes two diagonal covariance moments; differentiating F(a,b) proves every rational transfer entry, with denominator uniformly positive. The symmetric positive transfer has the displayed trace and determinant and Perron root, reached from every nonzero initial squared-coordinate vector. The conditional bound gap is a strict explicit polynomial identity for t>1. The bundled checker verifies 111 finite algebraic and quadrature instances; analytic proof establishes all parameters and iterations.

evidence: Gower et al. (2019), Theorem 2 gives a broad linear-convergence upper bound depending on the smallest eigenvalue of an expected projector.
Gower and Richtárik (2015), Theorem 8 bounds E[||error||^2] by rho^n times initial error; its Appendix B supplies rho for 2D Gaussian directions.
Fuji, Poirion and Takeda (2022) study regularized sketches and local convergence with a different update, not the exact deterministic quadratic directional minimization.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These published results cover broader classes of functions, dimensions or samplings in terms of rates and bounds, but neither their generality nor their proof implies the exact expected-objective equality at every n or the sharper Perron asymptotic coefficient. The existing sharp one-step upper bound remains correct and is not contradicted.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The method itself is equivalent to established random pursuit/sketch-and-project. The exact new claim is not algorithmic invention; it concerns E[ww^T C ww^T], a fourth moment of the random projection, whereas E[vv^T] is only a first matrix moment. The former cannot be reconstructed from the latter without additional identities, and its positive 2x2 transfer has a different asymptotic root than the one-step operator norm.

originality.rationale: The Gaussian random-direction update is already in 2011/2015/2019 literature. The inspected full-text results prove general expected-loss bounds and the exact first moment of the 2D Gaussian projector, but do not provide the squared-projector fourth-moment transfer or its universal sharp long-run objective Perron root. Those require the new covariance closure and moment evaluation; no directly covering stronger theorem was located in the comparisons, with specialist precedence risk expressly retained.
residual_risks: Equivalent sharp mean-square rates might be formulated in less-indexed planar random-projection or random-matrix-product publications; the comparison is not a complete field census.

The 2015 first-moment formula is very close to the moment calculation; novelty is claimed only for the full second-moment propagation and sharp long-run consequence, not for the underlying algorithm or first moment.

value.rationale: Random one-column exact Newton/line search is a natural benchmark for sketch-and-project optimization, and its true long-run expected loss can be substantially faster than the one-step guarantee. An exact all-initialization two-state moment propagation and the sharp 3/2 high-anisotropy improvement give a structural quantitative description of the error-direction feedback, not a mere first-moment rephrasing or arbitrary finite lookup. The value lies in exactness and a meaningful gap, without claiming a new general algorithm or guarantee.
